name: Linux Mint
packageManager: apt (Flatpak included, no Snap by default)
summary: A polished, traditional desktop built on Ubuntu LTS that feels familiar to Windows users.
bestFor: First-time Linux users who want something that just works.
cons: Software is not the newest, and the project is moving to a longer release cycle
Slower to adopt new desktop technology such as Wayland
verificationNote: Base, editions and no-Snap policy confirmed via news coverage of the Mint team. Mint 23 (Ubuntu 26.04 base) is planned for December 2026, so re-check then. Confirm on linuxmint.com before launch.

name: Ubuntu
summary: The most widely used desktop Linux, with a huge community and a new LTS every two years.
bestFor: Beginners who want the most support and tutorials available.
pros: Five years of free support on LTS releases
cons: Firefox and other default apps ship as Snaps, which some users dislike
Higher recommended hardware than lighter distros
Less customizable by default
verificationNote: 26.04 LTS released April 23, 2026 with 5 years of free support and GNOME 50 (no X11 session). Official flavors such as Kubuntu and Xubuntu exist separately.

name: Fedora Workstation
summary: A clean, modern distro backed by the Fedora Project that ships recent software on a roughly six-month cycle.
bestFor: People who want recent software without going fully rolling.
cons: Each release is supported for only about 13 months, so you upgrade at least yearly
Some media codecs need extra setup
verificationNote: Cycle, support length, GNOME default and KDE edition status confirmed via secondary sources. Re-check on fedoraproject.org before launch.

name: Debian
summary: The rock-solid foundation many other distros are built on, with a new stable release roughly every two years.
bestFor: Anyone who values stability above all and doesn't need the newest software.
pros: Five-year lifecycle: three years of full support plus two of LTS
cons: Software is older
Gaming and new hardware can need extra work
verificationNote: Official Debian pages confirm the 5-year lifecycle and the current stable release. Desktop list is general knowledge, not checked against the installer.

name: Pop!_OS
summary: A developer and gamer friendly distro from hardware maker System76.
bestFor: Gamers and developers, especially with Nvidia graphics.
cons: Tied to one company's direction
COSMIC is a new desktop (first stable release December 2025) and still maturing
verificationNote: 24.04 LTS with COSMIC stable released December 2025, built on Ubuntu 24.04. GPU-support claim comes from general knowledge and is not yet sourced.

name: Bazzite
packageManager: rpm-ostree, Flatpak, Homebrew (plus ujust helper commands)
summary: A gaming-focused, image-based system that's hard to break.
bestFor: Gamers who want a console-like, low-maintenance experience.
pros: Gaming tools preinstalled (Steam, Lutris and others)
Read-only system with atomic updates and easy rollbacks
Separate images with Nvidia drivers included
cons: Software is installed differently from traditional distros (Flatpak, Homebrew, layering)
Less flexible for deep system changes
verificationNote: Confirmed against Bazzite docs and repo: Fedora Atomic base, KDE and GNOME images, Steam Gaming Mode variants for handhelds and HTPCs.

name: Arch Linux
summary: A minimal, do-it-yourself rolling distro with excellent documentation and a guided installer.
bestFor: Experienced users who want full control and the newest software.
pros: archinstall guided installer on the official ISO
cons: You assemble the system yourself, including the desktop, even with archinstall
Rolling updates need regular attention (read Arch news before big upgrades)
verificationNote: Rolling release, pacman, AUR and archinstall confirmed via secondary sources. Re-check on archlinux.org before launch.

name: EndeavourOS
summary: Arch with a friendly graphical installer and a close-to-vanilla experience.
bestFor: People who want Arch's freshness without the manual install.
cons: Rolling releases need regular care
Terminal comfort helps
verificationNote: Arch base, Calamares installer, offline vs online install confirmed. Sources disagree on the default offline desktop (Xfce vs KDE Plasma), and Hyprland support was not confirmed, so it was removed. Check endeavouros.com before launch.

name: openSUSE Tumbleweed
summary: A tested rolling release with strong system snapshot and rollback tools.
bestFor: Users who want new software but a safety net when updates go wrong.
pros: Fresh software, tested by openQA before release
Btrfs and Snapper snapshots with rollback by default
cons: Smaller community than Ubuntu or Fedora
Official docs note a rolling release can occasionally ship a system-breaking update
verificationNote: Confirmed via openSUSE documentation and SUSE: rolling, zypper, Btrfs and Snapper by default, openQA testing.

name: NixOS
summary: Your whole system defined in config files: reproducible, rollback-friendly, with stable releases twice a year and a rolling unstable branch.
bestFor: Tinkerers and developers who want a fully reproducible setup.
cons: Steep learning curve
Unlike other distros, so tutorials often don't apply
verificationNote: Confirmed via NixOS wiki: declarative configuration, atomic upgrades and rollbacks, stable releases in late May and late November.
